newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar ends lower after reported RBNZ comment.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar ends lower after reported RBNZ comment.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed sharply lower on Thursday after Reserve Bank Governor Don Brash reportedly said the bank was reviewing whether its monetary conditions line was appropriate, dealers said.
The bank's March economic projections assumed a Trade-Weighted Index at 68.0 and 90-day bank bills at 7.5 percent.
Dealers said the RBNZ's assumed trade-off between the TWI and 90-days remained in force, but the bank was reviewing whether the line was still appropriate for its June monetary policy statement.
"It's come off about 35 points on the comments that came from Brash," a dealer said.
The Kiwi closed at US$0.6902/09 and at 68.58 on its Trade-Weighted Index, down from 0.6926/33 and 68.92 at the open.
